analysis.title: Stuck With The Bridge: Banks Shelve Junk Bond Sale For Anthropic's $15 Billion Texas Data Center After Abbott Freeze
key_insights: Banks led by Morgan Stanley delayed the sale of $5-7 billion of high-yield bonds meant to refinance part of a $15 billion loan funding an Anthropic-tied data center in Hubbard, Texas. Sales may now be staggered over the next year, so the banks hold the debt on balance sheet longer than planned.

The loan package is a $14.2 billion one-year loan (Citigroup, Intesa Sanpaolo, Mizuho, Morgan Stanley, MUFG, RBC, Santander) plus a $1.4 billion five-year revolver. Each bank committed about $2 billion to the loan and about $200 million to the revolver, with two extension options for up to one more year. The loan is already funded, and some banks including Santander are trying to bring in other lenders.

The project is developed by Nexus Data Centers and leased to Anthropic. Per the WSJ, Google guarantees billions of Anthropic's lease and power-payment obligations in exchange for a roughly 20% stake. The bond was rated in the mid-BB area.

The proximate cause is Texas Governor Abbott's data center freeze. On August 3 he ordered PUCT and ERCOT to audit every data center seeking a grid connection and paused approvals. On September 21 he directed TCEQ to stop issuing all data center-related permits until ERCOT finishes its review. Per Bracewell, the pause covers major air permits and reaches fully islanded, behind-the-meter projects.
Hubbard reportedly includes its own 1.6 GW natural gas plant, which now also needs a permit that is not being issued. Goldman sees behind-the-meter generation powering 25% of data centers by 2030.

ERCOT is auditing roughly 300 data centers of 75MW or more and aims to file findings with PUCT on December 10. It said it will not finish its large-load study by April 9, 2027. Public Citizen found at least 16 permits issued by TCEQ's automated portal after the directive, which were then suspended, and the portal was shut for manual screening. The article expects the freeze not to lift before year-end.

Goldman's KC O'Connor reports USD HY AI-related spreads widened 78bps over two weeks to a new high of 400bps over Treasuries, versus 22bps wider for non-AI HY excluding triple-Cs. The GS HY AI datacenter basket (GSHYAIDC) fell about 1pt last week, and there has been no new HY AI deal month-to-date in October.

BofA's 'Funding the Future #5' reports HY AI spreads surged 55bps week-to-date to record wides of 377bps. Over 25% of new-money issuance this year is AI-led, with AI-related issuance at $581 billion YTD.

Goldman's credit desk says the AI debate has shifted from how much capital is deployed to how much financing the market can absorb and who bears the risk. In IG tech the problem is the absence of natural buyers rather than aggressive selling.
The broader HY index average risk premium hit a 17-month high per Bloomberg, and triple-C spreads are at a four-year wide of 1,127bps per Goldman, with a spate of pulled deals in recent weeks.

Among 20 tracked data center junk bonds, smaller Google-backed deals trade at yields of 6.6% to 7.5%. Meridian's $5.7 billion 6.25% notes due 2031 with a Google lease guarantee trade at 91.4 cents and yield 8.6%, down almost 2 points since late September. Texas-sited bonds already operating (Black Pearl 6.5%, Stingray 7.0%, Cipher 7.1%, Flash 7.5%) sit at the tight end, so the issue is permitting risk on new builds, not Texas itself.
A $6 billion deal at about 8.5% implies roughly $500 million a year in interest, assuming buyers appear at Meridian's level.

Seven banks hold about $2.2 billion each in the Hubbard campus for at least a year. The author says this will not sink Morgan Stanley or MUFG but uses balance sheet capacity needed for later deals, while Goldman expects an active 2027 AI issuance year.

Related AI financing stress cited: Hock Tan personally guaranteed losses to finalize a $63 billion SPV financing of Anthropic's Broadcom chips after banks got cold feet. Oracle's Project Jupiter $18 billion 'Red Chile' term loans slid to stressed levels before force majeure. CoreWeave bonds fell earlier in October, and investment advisors quintupled AI datacenter bond holdings this year.

Anthropic filed its S-1 on Monday (Oct 26), with an $800 billion compute bill attached per the article. The author argues Hubbard is likely to become the template, with more bridge loans that stay on balance sheets and more deals needing a Google or Broadcom guarantee. The counter view is a timing problem that resolves after ERCOT signs off in December and the midterms on November 3.

tension_points.bull_case: A timing problem: once ERCOT signs off in December and the midterms pass, the bonds get sold, staggered or not. Smaller Google-backed deals still trade at 6.6% to 7.5%.
tension_points.bear_case: Hubbard becomes the template: more bridges that stay on bank balance sheets, deals needing a Google or Broadcom guarantee, AI HY spreads at record wides with no new AI deal in October, and a heavy 2027 supply calendar.
tension_points.what_invalidates: ERCOT audit findings due December 10 and a lifted TCEQ permit freeze would support the bull case. The bear case is supported by the freeze continuing past year-end or the first staggered bond sales pricing well below Meridian's 8.6% yield.

theme_stances.key_argument: Banks lend first and hand risk to bond investors, and the second leg failed in Hubbard because of Texas permitting and a junk market with no appetite for AI risk.
theme_stances.evidence: Hubbard becomes the template rather than the exception

theme_stances.key_argument: The TCEQ pause reaches even islanded, behind-the-meter projects, and the freeze is unlikely to lift before year-end.
theme_stances.evidence: even the power plant you build yourself now needs a permit that nobody is issuing
